- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to reflect risk-off bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak for next 3–5 days.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70–72), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.5% lag correction to forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-period moving average) to reduce volatility amplification.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– cycles (e.g., +0.67, -0.33, +0.67), model may misalign with trend; align forecast to sentiment-weighted average of recent 5–7 days.
